context: A tutor and two students discuss a group project on renewable energy adoption in rural communities.

lines.text: Now turn to Section Three. You will hear a tutor and two students discussing a group project.
Questions twenty-one to twenty-four. Complete the sentences. Write no more than three words for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-one to twenty-four.
So, Sofia, Ben — how's the renewable energy project coming along?
Good, I think. We've decided to focus on solar adoption in rural communities specifically.
Interesting choice. What made you narrow it down that way?
Honestly, it's because the cost barrier is much higher there, so we thought it'd be a more useful case study.
That's a solid rationale. How are you planning to gather your data?
We're planning to run interviews with about twenty households across two villages.
Good sample size. And when's the fieldwork happening?
We're heading out next month, so we've got about three weeks to prepare our questions.
Questions twenty-five to twenty-seven. Complete the summary. Write one word only for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-five to twenty-seven.
Now, what's your biggest concern going into the fieldwork itself?
For me, it's language — a few of the households only speak the local dialect, so we may need a translator.
That's a fair concern. Ben, what about you?
Mine's more about timing — harvest season overlaps with our visit, so people might be too busy to talk to us.
Good thinking ahead. And what's your backup plan if that happens?
We'd shift to evenings, since that's when people are usually home.
Questions twenty-eight to thirty. Complete the notes. Write no more than three words for each answer. First, you have some time to look at questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Now listen and answer questions twenty-eight to thirty.
Now, in terms of the report itself — Sofia, which part are you writing?
I've got the data analysis section.
And Ben, yours?
I'm doing the introduction and the recommendations at the end.
Sounds well divided. When's the full draft due?
We're aiming for the end of next month.
Great, that all sounds on track. Let's check in again once you're back from the field.
Sounds good, thank you.
That is the end of Section Three. Now turn to Section Four.
